key_insight: A fifth-order Taylor state-evolution scheme replaces costly matrix exponentiation in adaptive VQE, turning ansatz growth into a sequence of sparse matrix-vector multiplies.
engineering_relevance: This reduces classical memory and compute bottlenecks in large-scale quantum chemistry simulations, making ADAPT-VQE more practical on constrained HPC resources.
method: Use deterministic O(5) Taylor expansion for state updates
Perform five successive sparse matrix-vector multiplications with O(Nz) scaling
evidence_signal: Across BeH2, H2O, and stretched H2O under JW and BK mappings, the method achieved >0.999999 fidelity and subchemical-accuracy ground-state energies while handling matrices with over 268 million structural elements.
watch_item: A truncated Taylor scheme may require step-size or convergence checks to ensure stability and accuracy on harder instances or deeper ansatz growth.
paper_title: Alleviating the Sparse Matrix Scaling Bottleneck in Adaptive VQE via High-Order Taylor State Evolution
